measuredFidelity.note: The rig's 6.75-degree leg splay (render.leg-stance) settled ankle daylight at 48.5% against the concept's 46.9%. Round 7 then found that Junebug's SIGNATURE idle pose carried an 8-degree inward leg roll, authored when the rig ran its legs straight down, which closed the ankles to 0.325ft against the bind pose's 0.756 and failed rubric 3.12 in idle while the bind-pose render this command reads stayed correct. The same roll was in all five signature idles and was removed from all of them; an FK sweep now reads every idle within 2% of bind. Re-measured 2026-08-12 after the detector itself was rebuilt to work for the whole roster: the backdrop is now sampled per column (seven sheets are vignetted past the old tolerance), a column counts as occupied by fraction rather than by any single pixel, and the shoe's two tones are read off the concept instead of the hardcoded red/cream that was Junebug's own shoe. Her shoe deltas TIGHTENED, from +2.23/+2.93 under the old classifier to +0.43/-0.78 as tone shares (41.2/25.5 concept against 41.6/24.8 delivered); the round-7 critic note below quotes the old red/cream figures and is left as the record of what was measured then.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is right and it is right by measurement, not by eye: head 34.0% of figure height against the turnaround's 33.9% (+0.10), head width:height 0.82 against 0.84, ankle daylight 48.5 against 46.9. With colour stripped she is still unmistakably the scowling kid with a bun, a headband and a swept tail. Held off 5 by butt-joined primitives, and I re-observed all three the round-7 critic named, each cropped at 4-10x from the region I cite. (1) BUN/CROWN SHELF, junebug-front-review.png x 220-330 y 55-115: the bun sits on the crown ring with a hard vertical step at BOTH silhouette edges and a shadow line across its base — no fillet, a visible corner, dead centre in the front view. (2) HEADBAND STUB, junebug-profile-review.png x 285-370 y 55-165 at 10x over a magenta backdrop: the band's rear end is a flat-cut rectangle terminating in silhouette against true background, where the concept sweeps it behind the ear to the nape. (3) PONYTAIL TIP, x 290-520 y 40-310: the tail tube ends on a flat circular cut and a separate smaller blob is stuck onto it, the seam a full crease ring with a notch either side, against a concept tip that tapers to a drawn arrowhead. A fourth: the pelvis is a flat-bottomed slab that overhangs the thigh tubes with a hard horizontal ledge across the whole hip, visible on the front board at 4x (x 180-360 y 370-420) and on both profile boards. Nothing is severed — a connected-component pass over all four boards returns exactly one component each.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is exact and measured, not asserted: head height delta +0.10 points, head aspect -0.02, ankle daylight +1.61 — every 6b metric inside tolerance, and the head:body read is the turnaround's, never the proxy's. The A-pose boards hold the drawn stance with the arms down and daylight between the thighs and calves, so 3.12 passes on the board and again in the run still. The second clause of the 4 bar — 'joints read as connected forms' — is where it stops. The pelvis-to-thigh is the offender: build_leg's top ring simply terminates at 1.72ft inside a separately built seat, so at 4x on both the front and profile boards you see a slab overhanging a narrower tube with a lip, not a hip. The knee is nearly formless too — the ring table runs 0.180 at the knee against 0.172 just above it, a 5% swell that renders as a straight tapering cylinder in profile. It stays a 4 because the joints that carry motion hold: the run still shows a round deltoid under the sleeve cap, a continuous elbow line and a knee that bends without tearing, and the jersey hem covers the pelvis ledge at every gameplay camera.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The one category below the floor, and the deciding clause is the 4 bar's own words: 'one designed mass'. What ships is four stacked primitives with five visible joins. MEASURED first. Default band (5-45% of head height) reads 1.38 minima/row against the concept's 3.82 — 36% of the strand count at 146% of the prominence. That band is not trustworthy on this kid: on both sheets it spans the headband, whose two edges count as FALSE creases, so I re-ran it on a hair-only band. At 2-14% (bun crest and crown, above the band on both sheets) the concept reads 3.00 minima/row and the delivered reads 0.04 — 1% of the concept's strand count. At 2-22%, 1%. At 2-30%, 8%. The bun is a mathematically featureless dome, which the rubric caps at 4 on its own. Then the joins. (a) The bun butt-joins the crown on a hard shelf with a corner at both silhouette edges (front board 10x, x 220-330 y 55-115) and the toon outline pass draws it as a graphic line at gameplay scale in junebug-runtime-hero.png. (b) The hair tie is a FLAT QUAD SLAB, not a wrap: at 10x over magenta it is a single plane crossing in front of the tail whose lower edge is a hard flat cut with true background beneath it, and at gameplay scale in the run still it reads as a yellow tab stuck to the side of the head. (c) True background — alpha 0, sampled at (310,72) and (315,80) of junebug-profile-review.png — shows through the notch between the bun and the ponytail root, so the two masses do not touch; the tail hangs off the head through a narrow neck below the tie. (d) The tip blob. The 4 clauses it does pass are real and worth saying: the hairline is a proper sculpted widow's-peak that reads clean against skin from the front, there is no bare-skull read from any angle, and the headband arch itself is the best-authored accessory on the sheet.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The strongest sculpted category. Garments read as constructed at 5x on the A-pose board: the V-collar is a rounded piping TUBE rather than a painted line, the placket carries three raised button studs, the sleeves have two white stripes plus a real white cuff band, the belt is a band with two loops and a buckle, the knicker gathers into a darker cuff, the sock has its own band, and the shoe has a distinct lighter midsole slab and a red toe cap. The shoe's split is measured, not eyeballed: dominant tone 63.7% of the band against the concept's 64.7, second tone 31.1 against 27.2, mean saturation 34.9 against 36.8. Off 5 on the laces, which are three raised rectangular slabs on the vamp — they do not cross, have no eyelets and no weave, and on the right shoe of the front board one slab breaks the shoe's silhouette (x 160-390 y 590-710 at 4x). Secondary: the jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The face is a FORM, and I checked the specific things that separate a form from a sticker. A real nose breaks the profile with a defined tip and a nostril underside (junebug-profile-review.png x 210-320 y 110-240 at 8x). No decal-island seam anywhere — I looked for one at 8-10x on both the front and the profile and the atlas wraps the cheek and temple planes continuously. The ears are the best-constructed detail on the whole model: outer helix rim, inner concha shadow, and a lobe sitting against the skull, which settles 3.10 with no ambiguity. Features are legible at hero scale and the angled scowl brows still read at 40px. The chest patch I thought was a texture island at 4x is a specular gradient — resolved at 10x, not a defect. Held off 5 by the mouth. At rest it is a thin flat stroke a few pixels tall, close to the 'collapses to a line' the rubric warns about, and the expression RANGE does not survive: I pixel-diffed a 46x36 mouth box across the four runtime stills and grin/cheer/tongue are the same mouth (grin vs cheer 99 of 4968 channels differ by more than 12, max 39; cheer vs tongue 202, max 70) while only angry is distinct (650-669, max 120). Cropping the source atlas confirms it is the asset, not the capture instrument: cells 1, 10 and 11 are three near-identical open smiles, so the tongue cell has no tongue out and the cheer cell is no wider than the grin. All four stills are genuinely painted — byte sizes 291673/291988/292081/292276, a 0.2% spread, and all four show grass, sky and the character.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives both ends. At hero (junebug-runtime-hero.png, devstats reads 'model model', so this is the delivered GLB and not proxy evidence) the read is complete: scowl brows, big eyes, white headband arch, dark bun, tail swept to her left. I generated my own 40px read by resizing the front board to 40px tall, and every load-bearing element holds — dark bun over a white band, red top, pink pants, red socks, white shoes, and the angled brows are still two dark marks that say 'determined'. Off 5 on two counts. First, in the FRONT view at field scale the ponytail is entirely hidden behind her, so at 40px she is a bun-and-headband kid and the signature tail — the thing the turnaround draws an arrow at — contributes nothing to the read from the camera the fielder is most often seen from. Second, the tie reads at hero as a flat yellow tab rather than a wrap (junebug-runtime-run.png x 415-595 y 140-290 at 6x), which is a hero-scale accessory defect, not a hair-only one.

The six category scores recorded here are the round-7 independent critic's, not the sculptor's.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Holds at 2. The hero read improved - the swept crown plus chair is a distinctive one-glance identity - but the 40px field read is still dominated by the chair's missing mass, which was out of scope this round.

measuredFidelity.result: Same detector run on concept and delivery throughout. Profile sweep (share of above-crown hair mass rearward of skull-centre x): concept 82.5%, delivered 80.9% - swept-back confirmed, splay gone. Front splay (tip-band avg width / root-band avg width above the crown line): concept 0.45, delivered 0.27 - tips inside roots, no radial read. Head aspect, hair+skin box ears included, crown-top to 55%-width chin: concept 0.984, delivered 1.107 (delta +0.123); crown-above-brow height 0.76x face height on the sheet vs 0.60x delivered - the claimed 1.05-vs-1.06 match does not reproduce on this instrument, and the residual is crown HEIGHT, not width. Crown colour in game light: dark-mass mean RGB (45,45,40) frontal / (31,29,22) hero vs concept crown (46,41,37) - neutral-warm, matching; lit facets mean (117,113,101), red>blue, i.e. warm-grey not steel-blue; but pale-facet share of hair area is 11.8% frontal vs the concept's 4.5%, and 34.6% of dark frontal crown pixels still carry a b>r+6 cool cast. Sources confirm ten lock spines (three mirrored pairs + two centre + one mid pair), 7-sided tubes, sweep authored in +y with side-lock tips at x ±0.61/±0.44.
measuredFidelity.note: featurelatitude gates brow 56.2, eye 71.6 (bounded crop traces), mouth 83.5 (the analyser's own trace). NO earLine target - Zippy's precedent, the spike crown owns the widest rows on both the sheet and any delivery. The sheet is seated in every view so the analyser's z frame is chair-relative; only percent-of-head landmarks carry. The chair, tucked legs and shoes are ROOT-weighted furniture (the proxy's proven approach); the blue push rims are the team accent.

polishFindings: PRIMARY. The chair is half the mass the sheet gives it and sits too low on the figure: measured 43.6% lower-40% fill against the concept's 83.7%, chair top 61.1% down against 44.9%, chair width 43.4% of figure height against ~60%. Raise the seat/wheel assembly relative to the hip so the wheel tops reach his elbow as they do on the sheet, and thicken the seat, backrest and rails until the front board's lower half is a dense black-and-blue mass rather than open scaffolding. Everything else on this list is downstream of it. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The drive wheels read as flat parallel-sided black slabs with square-cut faceted ends in the front board, not as cambered ellipses. The camber is authored (WHEEL_CAMBER 0.115) but at 16 ring points and a 0.060 tube it does not survive the orthographic front view. Either increase the camber or give the tyre enough ring points that the lean reads as a curve. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The four frame rails per side terminate in tapered points hanging in mid-air (rail 1 ends at z 0.300, radius 0.036, i.e. z 0.264 with ground at 0) and cross in an unresolved X in the front board. Close the chassis: join the rails into axle bosses and a caster fork so no tube ends in space. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The METAL footplate ellipsoid is buried inside the WHITE sole tube (sole bottom z 0.343 vs footplate top z 0.423) and pokes out through the outboard side of the sneaker as a bare grey stub at hero scale - a 3.8 interpenetration. Drop the footplate ~0.06 so it sits under the sole, which also makes it read in profile, where it currently reads as absent. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The caster is an open torus (ring radius 0.130, tube radius 0.040) so the field shows through its middle at hero scale. The sheet's caster is a solid small wheel with a blue hub - fill the centre. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The push rim, the only team-accent geometry on the asset, survives the front board as a 2px hairline, so the team read depends entirely on the 3/4 camera. Extent, not colour - widen or move it outboard of the tyre silhouette. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

RE-VERIFIED, HOLDS. The sneakers deliver none of the sheet's construction: no toe, no heel, no ankle collar, no teal velcro straps, and the two-tone sole is 0.00% of the shoe band against the concept's 13.3%. build_seated_legs is unchanged this round (one SHOE tube plus one WHITE sole tube); the runtime hero still shows a plain blue lozenge on a white slab.

RE-VERIFIED, HOLDS. The shin is a near-constant dowel from knee to ankle (authored radii 0.085/0.078/0.072) with no calf and no ankle, and the knee is a butt joint with a visible diameter step under the hem lip; the navy thigh still reads as a hard-topped box in the run and swing stills. Untouched this round.

RE-VERIFIED, HOLDS. The skull is an undifferentiated sphere with no jaw or cheekbone and the nose is a shallow button, so the otherwise excellent face reads as painted onto a ball at the near-front gameplay angle. This is what holds face/expression at 4 rather than 5. The face window did move in (0.28/0.40) and the brows stay clear of the fringe - that half is fine.

MEASURED CLEAR. Prior finding 'seven flat blades too deep/too few at 390% prominence' no longer holds: the crown-band ring wave was dropped entirely (the 16-column shell reads as a smooth scalp, per the sheet) and the spike count went to ten grouped locks. No column flutes visible in the front or profile board at 8x.

MEASURED CLEAR. Prior finding 'fins splay radially where the sheet sweeps the mass up and rearward, temples bare' no longer holds: profile sweep measures 80.9% of above-crown hair mass rearward vs the concept's 82.5% (same detector), front tip/root width ratio is 0.27 vs the concept's own 0.45 (tips inside roots - the hedgehog is dead), and the fringe now descends past ear-top at both temples. The sweep was moved into y exactly as claimed and it worked.

PARTIAL CLEAR, REFINED. The steel-BLUE glint is gone: lit hair facets now average RGB (117,113,101) - warm grey, red above blue - and the dark mass means (45,45,40) frontal / (31,29,22) hero against the concept crown's (46,41,37). What remains is a pale-TIP band: at the frontal gameplay angle the five centre spike tips catch full sun and flatten to light grey, 11.8% of hair area vs the concept crown's 4.5%, reading as grey-tipped hair on a near-black crown (zoom-runtime-face-angry.png, crop at 3x). 34.6% of dark frontal crown pixels also still carry a slight cool cast (b > r+6), visible as a slate sheen on the fringe band's facets. This is a normals/roughness question on the 7-sided tips, not a swatch question - same caveat as before re the tonemapping gate.

NEW. The head-aspect claim does not reproduce: with one instrument on both images (hair+skin box, ears included, crown-top to the 55%-width chin row), the concept front measures 0.984 w:h and the delivered front board 1.107 - a +0.123 delta, and the miss is HEIGHT: crown-above-brow is 0.60x face height delivered vs 0.76x on the sheet. The shallower locks fixed the splay but gave back ~20% of the sheet's crown rise. Before touching geometry, reconcile instruments - the sculptor's ladder read 1.06/1.05 on measure:fidelity - but if any rise is added, add it to the two centre locks' z, not to lateral tips.

NEW, MINOR. The locks are dead-straight 3-point spines, so in profile the crown reads as a stack of parallel flat knives at one shared rake angle - a venetian-blind read where the sheet's locks curve and vary their sweep. A slight bow in each spine (middle point pushed 0.03-0.05 off the root-tip chord, varied per lock) would break the parallelism for zero extra segments.

NEW, NOTE ONLY - probably not actionable. The x-mirror constraint (faceAsymmetry gate) makes the two ±0.61 side locks read as a matched pair of lateral horns in the front board, where the sheet's front view is an asymmetric tousle leaning to his right. This is the rig-wide symmetry trade every character makes; recorded so the next critic does not file the horn-pair as a defect.

VERIFIED, NOT REPRODUCED - the earlier finding that 'the backrest ellipsoid (y 0.300, half-depth 0.065, z 1.740) floats behind the tee with visible daylight in the hero, run and swing stills' does NOT hold on the regenerated evidence. Cropped at 8x on zoom-profile-review.png, zoom-runtime-hero.png, zoom-runtime-run.png and zoom-runtime-swing.png, the backrest slab abuts the torso's back edge with only the toon outline between them and no background pixel showing through in any of the four. That earlier review ran on stale stills. The backrest's real problem is that it is a thin lens too small to read as a chair back, not that it floats. [KEPT - non-defect record]

FALSE FINDING I ALMOST FILED, recorded so the next reviewer does not file it: in zoom-profile-review.png the collar carries what looks at 8x like a skin-coloured disc bearing two brow strokes and a mouth - a second face on his chest. It is not. The front board is a T-pose, so in a true 90-degree profile the near arm points at the camera and what you are seeing is the teal sleeve cuff ring with the foreshortened hand inside it, the 'brows' being finger gaps. Same class as the foreshortened near-side eye. Benign. [KEPT - non-defect record]

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The one thing this character is named for is measurably short. His tee at its widest is 28.9% of figure height (162px/561) against the concept's 34.0% (244px/717) - 15% narrow; in profile his torso is 24.8% deep at pct 58 against the concept's 29.9% at pct 56 - 17% shallow. Cross-section therefore carries roughly 70% of the concept's bulk, and the side-by-side at matched scale reads as a normal-build kid wearing a padded shirt rather than a heavy kid. Worse, the profile at 5x shows the tee is a hard-cornered BOX: a flat front face, a flat side face and a hard vertical crease between them running the full height of the garment, plus a flat horizontal hem cut. Rule 3.1's 5/5 forbids butt-joined primitives; this is below that - the primitive joins are visible in the silhouette itself. Two things I want on record as PASSING so nobody re-files them: legs are two legs (I measured max inter-leg daylight 35.0% of row span at pct 96, 34.2% at 94, 32.4% at 92, against the concept front figure's 33.0% at 88 and 26.6% at 90 - his legs are correct and I confirmed the leg thickness matches too, 10.2% of figH per leg vs the concept's 10.3%), and nothing is severed anywhere in board or runtime. Against those, the misses: ears are the widest point of the entire head silhouette, protruding ~15px per side beyond the skull, and the head reads max-width/head-height 1.12 vs the concept front figure's 0.97 measured the same way; the nose does not break the profile (3.2% of head height vs the concept's 10.3%, below); the shorts are 30% short (8.4% of figH vs 12.1%); the shoe upper is less than half the concept's height (2.7% of figH vs 6.0%), turning a chunky sneaker into a flat slipper. 2.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The best category and still not at the floor. The AUTO metrics are genuinely fine - measure:fidelity reports head height 27.9% vs concept 26.1% (+1.73, ok) and head width:height 1.10 vs 1.06 (+0.04, ok) - and I independently confirmed the legs are correctly thick, so the gross child proportion is right and this is not a proxy read. What fails is the second half of the rule, 'joints read as connected forms'. The shoulder is a truncated sleeve cone butted onto a flat shoulder plane: at 8x and 10x on the runtime hero and run stills there is a broken, dotted dark outline arc running from the collar out over the deltoid and down into the armpit, which is the toon outline firing on a shell intersection, and the diameter steps visibly where the sleeve ends and the bare arm begins - no round deltoid form survives. The elbow in swing_contact is a hard crease with a dark notch, two cylinders meeting at an angle, and the two forearms interpenetrate with a hard intersection line where they cross. The hand is a merged paddle with a single thumb nub and three shallow finger notches; in the profile A-pose it reads as a mitten. The neck is also a distinct visible cylinder with a collar ring above it, where the concept Big Lou has essentially no neck at all - his head sits straight on his shoulders, and that missing compression costs part of the 'big' read. 3.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I ran measure:strands at four bands to be sure the finding was not an artifact of the default band reaching onto forehead and brows - 5-45% (the default), 5-28%, 3-22% and 2-18%. Every band says the same thing: delivered carries 52%, 43%, 38% and 33% of the concept's strand-minima count while carrying 204%, 204%, 183% and 175% of its prominence. That is the exact signature of a smooth mass with a handful of deep chunky gouges standing in for a dense fine grain, which rule 3.3 caps at 4 even when the silhouette is right - and here the silhouette is not right either. The concept is a tight buzz cut that hugs the skull with a faded temple and a clean straight hairline; the delivered hair is a thick bowl/mushroom helmet with real volume standing off the back of the skull, a hard front edge over the forehead, and a jagged stair-stepped notch at each temple where the hairline meets the sideburn (visible at 5x in the profile crop). The mass is designed as one piece, it reads front and side, and there is no bare-skull read from any angle I checked, so it clears the floor items - but it is the wrong haircut rendered as a featureless blob. 2.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real credit first, because two things here are better than the rest of the asset: the shoe is genuinely constructed - cream toe cap, navy quarter, cream midsole, a dark outsole line and a short dark lace mark, all separately readable at 5x - and the sock has an actual cuff roll rather than a plain tube. Everything else fails. The stripe pitch is wrong by a large measured margin: 20px on a 561px figure (3.6% of figure height) against the concept's 37px on a 717px figure (5.2%), a 31% finer pitch, and because the delivered tee is also taller the band count over the garment is ~10 against the concept's ~5. Every stripe boundary is a soft ~4px vertex-colour gradient, not a constructed edge - I sampled a column at x=270 in the front A-pose and the transitions blur over four native pixels; the concept's are crisp. The tee is the box described above with no side seam, no sleeve cuff and no drape. The shorts are two flat-faced slabs with hard corners, no hem cuff, no waistband and no pocket, and they are 30% short (waistband matches the concept exactly at 64.7% vs 64.6% of figure height, but the hem lands at 73.1% against 76.7%). Under the shirt hem at the crotch there is a hard-edged near-black rectangle roughly 21x2 native px - I cropped that exact region at 16x and it is a flat black slab with crisp edges and no gradient, so it is not occlusion falloff; it is either a see-through gap or an untextured polygon, and it is the only 3.7 candidate I found. 2.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Two traps checked and cleared before scoring. Ears: I grepped the sculpt script and found `from sculptlib.ear import EarSpec, build_ear` with `EAR_SPEC = EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.420), radii=(0.1600, 0.1700))`, and at 5x on the profile board the ear has an outer helix rim, a concha depression with an inner shadow and a lobe against the skull - 3.10 PASSES. Mouth: all four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted and genuinely distinct - grin is a closed smile with a teeth line, cheer is an open mouth with teeth and a dark throat, tongue is an open mouth with a pink tongue out, angry is angled brows over a downturned frown - and all four read at draft-card distance, so 3.14 PASSES. What fails is the form. The nose is authored as a soft displacement (`nose_push`, 'a broad soft button nose') rather than built geometry, and it shows: in the profile board the front edge runs 213,213,213,212,211,209,208,210,213,216 across the nose latitude - a 5px bump on a 155px head, 3.2% of head height, against the concept profile figure's 19px bump on a 185px head, 10.3%. Rule 3.5's 5/5 asks that a real nose break the profile; measured, it barely dents it, and in all four front expression stills the nose is invisible - eyes, brows, mouth, then blank cheek. The brows are angular dark slabs with hard straight lower edges whose outer ends abut and merge into the hairline, where the concept's are tapered arcs with clear forehead above them. And the ear is authored at radii 0.170 against head radius 0.520, i.e. 32.7% of head height (I measured 31% off the board) against the concept's 24% - about 35% oversize - which is why at the runtime hero camera, with the head turned away, the dominant feature of the close-up is a giant protruding ear disc and not the face at all. 2.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: This is where the asset actually dies. I cropped the board's own 40-pixel zoom strip at 8x: the gold stripes are completely gone and the tee is a single undifferentiated cream blob. That is arithmetic, not opinion - a 20px band pitch on a 561px render is 1.4px per band at 40px height, below what the strip can resolve, and it is the direct consequence of the doubled stripe count under clothingConstruction. The one thing a child is meant to recognise Big Lou by on the field - bold broad gold-and-cream stripes on a wide round body - survives neither half of the read: the stripes alias away, and the silhouette is 15% narrow and 17% shallow so he does not read as a big kid either. At 40px he is a generic beige-shirted child. The hero read is separately weak: the ear dominates the close-up as described, the torso shows plainly faceted low-poly quads across the belly with visible shading discontinuities at 3x, and the shoulder-cap specular blows out over roughly 50 of the torso's 195 rows on both sides, erasing the stripe pattern exactly where the eye lands first. 3.9 FAILS. 2.

measuredFidelity.result:
measure:fidelity -- big_lou (concept front 330x712, delivered 451x560): head height 26.1 -> 27.9 (+1.73, ok); head w:h 1.06 -> 1.10 (+0.04, ok); shoe band dominant tone 82.7 -> 79.7 (-3.01, ok); shoe band second tone 16.3 -> 20.3 (+4.00, ok); shoe band mean saturation 16.9 -> 15.9 (-0.92, ok); daylight between ankles 0.00 -> 26.4 (+26.4, OFF tol 12 - this is 6b.4's bind-pose-vs-posed-drawing comparison, the concept front figure stands ankles together, so I read it as stance and did not widen anything); visible face left of centre 47.7 -> 44.2 (ok); right of centre 39.6 -> 44.2 (ok); face L/R asymmetry 0.00 -> 0.00 (ok). 1 metric outside tolerance.

measure:strands -- big_lou at four bands (stating the band because the 5-45% default reaches onto forehead and brows on a buzz cut): band 5-45% (default) concept 6.31 minima/row @ prominence 28.8 over 86 rows, delivered 3.27 @ 57.8 over 63 rows => 52% count / 201% prominence. Band 5-28%: 5.72 @ 15.5 vs 2.47 @ 31.7 => 43% / 204%. Band 3-22%: 6.00 @ 15.4 vs 2.30 @ 28.1 => 38% / 183%. Band 2-18%: 6.71 @ 14.8 vs 2.23 @ 25.8 => 33% / 175%. Every band agrees: far too few strand minima, far too deep.

My own measurements (concept front figure top y=106 bot y=822, figH=717px; delivered front/profile board top y=86 bot y=646, figH=561px; concept profile figure figH=722px):
- Inter-leg daylight, max gap as % of row span: delivered 32.4% @ pct92, 34.2% @ pct94, 35.0% @ pct96; concept front 28.4% @ pct86, 33.0% @ pct88, 26.6% @ pct90. Legs PASS, independently confirmed.
- Single-leg width: delivered 57px = 10.2% of figH @ pct80; concept 74px = 10.3% @ pct80. Match.
- Tee max width: delivered 162px = 28.9% of figH @ pct57; concept 244px = 34.0% @ pct57-59 (hue-32-55 shirt mask, background excluded). -15%.
- Profile torso max depth: delivered 24.8% of figH @ pct58 (peak of 23.5/24.6/24.6/24.8/24.6 across pct50-60); concept profile 29.9% @ pct56 (28.1/28.9/29.6/29.9/29.8 across pct50-58). -17%.
- Stripe pitch, front A-pose column x=270, band boundaries at y = 251,268,288,308,328,349,369,390,410,429 => pitch 20px on figH 561 = 3.6% of figH; concept column x=210, boundaries at y = 403,438,477,516,552 => pitch 35/39/39/36, mean 37.3px on figH 717 = 5.2% of figH. Delivered pitch 31% finer; band count over the tee ~10 vs ~5. At 40px figure height that is 1.4px per band -> stripes gone (verified by cropping the board's own 40px strip at 8x).
- Stripe edge softness: cream<->gold transition spans ~4 native px at 561px figure. Painted gradient, not a constructed edge.
- Shorts: navy run on both leg columns, delivered 64.7-73.1% of figure height (8.4% long); concept 64.6-76.7% and 65.0-76.7% (12.1% long). Waistband matches, hem 30% short.
- Shoe navy upper: delivered 93.6-96.3% of figure (2.7%); concept 89.5-95.5% (6.0%). Less than half height.
- Nose, profile front-edge x per row across the nose latitude: delivered 213,213,213,212,211,209,208,210,213,216 -> 5px protrusion on a 155px head = 3.2% of head height; concept 795,795,794,793,789,780,777,777,775,775,776,780 -> 19px on a 185px head = 10.3%. Delivered nose protrudes under one third as far.
- Head: delivered max head width 174px on head band 86-241 (155px) = 1.123 w:h measured my way; concept max head width 197px on head band 106-310 (204px) = 0.966. Delivered ~16% wider relative to its own height, and the excess is ears.
- Ear: vertical extent ~48px on a 155px head = 31% of head height; concept ear ~52px on a 213px head = 24%. Sculpt script authors EAR_SPEC radii (0.160, 0.170) against HEAD_RADII (0.500, 0.500, 0.520) = 32.7% of head height, confirming the board. Ear protrudes ~15px per side beyond the skull and is the widest point of the head silhouette.
- Crotch black slab: cropped at 16x, a flat near-black rectangle ~21x2 native px between the shirt hem and the shorts, crisp-edged with no gradient.
- Colour: on the fidelity board the gold stripe modal saturation is ~0.4 against the concept's ~0.8, but the runtime stills show the tee at full mustard - so this is board lighting, NOT a palette defect, and I am NOT filing it. Team accent is the sock roll-top (TEAM_MASK = E8DCC2, 'the sock roll-top - THE accent'), not the tee, so no colour judgement was made on any grey surface.
- Severed parts: none. Head, neck, torso, both arms, both hands, both legs and both feet are continuous in the front board, profile board, both A-pose boards and all three runtime clip stills.
- Shoulder/sleeve junction: no fin shear. What is there is a broken, dotted dark outline arc where the sleeve shell intersects the torso shell, visible at 8x and 10x on hero and run.
- Sleeve stripe alignment: checked and CLEARED. Columns x=205 (sleeve) and x=270/335 (torso) in the front A-pose share band boundaries at y=369, 389, 410 and 429 exactly; the apparent offset higher up is a blown-out specular highlight on the sleeve cap, not a mis-registered stripe.
- Four runtime-face stills: all genuinely painted and all four distinct (grin closed-smile with teeth line; cheer open with teeth and dark throat; tongue open with pink tongue; angry angled brows over frown). 3.14 PASSES.
measuredFidelity.note: featurelatitude gates brow 32.2, eye 47.7, mouth 73.9, earLine 51.8 - ALL hand-set bounded traces: the analyser refused his pinch outright ('no-pinch', the chunky chin-merges-into-neck class) so the neck row is hand-set at 305 (the collar line), and brow/eye/mouth all refused as merged regions. Deep skin chroma-authored 9C5428 (darkened from A65C2E after the round-2 critic) per the Grizz lesson.

polishFindings: Widen and deepen the torso: the tee is 28.9% of figure height wide against the concept's 34.0% and 24.8% deep in profile against 29.9%. Big Lou is the only heavy kid on the roster and roughly 30% of his cross-section is missing.

Round the tee. In profile at 5x it is a box - flat front face, flat side face, a hard vertical crease between them running the garment's full height, and a flat horizontal hem cut. Rule 3.1's 5/5 forbids butt-joined primitives and this is visible in the silhouette itself.

Halve the stripe count. Pitch 3.6% of figure height vs the concept's 5.2%, ~10 bands over the tee vs ~5, which is 1.4px per band at the 40px field read - the stripes disappear entirely and he becomes a generic beige-shirted kid. This is the single worst defect in the asset.
Harden the stripe boundaries: cream<->gold currently blends over ~4 native px, a painted vertex-colour gradient rather than a constructed edge.
Build the nose as geometry rather than a `nose_push` displacement. It protrudes 3.2% of head height in profile against the concept's 10.3% and is invisible in all four front expression stills.

Shrink the ears by about a third: authored EAR_SPEC radii 0.170 vs head radius 0.520 = 32.7% of head height, measured 31% on the board, against the concept's 24%. They are currently the widest point of the head and they dominate the runtime hero close-up.
Re-cut the hair as a buzz. It is a bowl/mushroom helmet standing off the back of the skull where the concept hugs it, with a hard front edge and a jagged stair-stepped temple notch visible at 5x.
Add strand grain to the hair: 33-52% of the concept's strand count at every band tested, at 175-204% of its prominence - a smooth mass with a few deep gouges instead of a dense fine grain.
Lengthen the shorts to mid-thigh: hem at 73.1% of figure height vs the concept's 76.7% (30% short). Waistband is already correct at 64.7% vs 64.6%.

Raise the shoe upper: navy quarter spans 2.7% of figure height vs the concept's 6.0%, so the chunky sneaker reads as a flat slipper. The toe cap, midsole, outsole and lace mark are all good - only the height is wrong.

Investigate the flat near-black ~21x2px rectangle under the shirt hem at the crotch (front A-pose board). Cropped at 16x it has crisp edges and no gradient, so it is not occlusion falloff - either a see-through gap or an untextured polygon.

Fix the sleeve/torso shell intersection: it emits a broken dotted dark outline arc from collar to armpit in the hero and run stills, and the diameter steps where the sleeve ends and the bare arm begins - no round deltoid form survives (3.11).

Give the elbow and wrist real forms. In swing_contact the elbow is a hard hinge crease with a dark notch, the two forearms interpenetrate with a visible hard intersection line, and the hand is a merged paddle with one thumb nub.
Compress the neck. A visible cylinder plus a collar ring sits where the concept has effectively no neck at all, and that alone costs part of the 'big' read.

Reframe the runtime hero shot or reduce the head yaw: at the current hero camera the head is turned far enough that the ear, not the face, is the dominant feature, so the hero still is not usable face evidence.
Tame the shoulder-cap specular: it blows out roughly 50 of the torso's 195 rows on both sides in the front A-pose board, erasing the stripe pattern exactly where the eye lands first.
Subdivide the belly: plainly faceted low-poly quads with visible shading discontinuities read across the torso at 3x in the runtime hero.

NOT DEFECTS, recorded so they are not re-filed: legs are two legs (35.0% max inter-leg daylight vs the concept's 33.0-36%) and leg thickness matches (10.2% vs 10.3% of figH); ears are constructed with rim, concha and lobe (`build_ear`/`EAR_SPEC` present); nothing is severed anywhere; all four face stills are painted and distinct; the sleeve stripes are correctly registered to the torso's (boundaries coincide at y=369/389/410/429); and the board's washed-out gold is board lighting, not a palette slip - the runtime stills show full mustard.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The gross read is right (egg dome, big round glasses, noodle neck, boxy striped tee, straight jeans, rolled cuffs) and the proportion metrics are green, but the two forms the sculpt script itself says 'carry the whole silhouette' both fail. (1) THE EARS DO NOT REACH THE OUTLINE. I measured the delivered front render (540x720, figure bbox y88-647): the head silhouette is widest at 162px at y187 - the DOME - and the ears break the outline only at rows 221-222, by 10px per side. At the traced ear line (57.9% of the 88->260 head band = y188) the right ear's outer edge is x342 while the skull edge is x349, so the ear is 7px INSIDE the outline and contributes nothing. The concept is the opposite: its head is widest AT THE EARS (229px at y252-262 vs 189px at y235 just above them), the ears exceed the skull for 60 rows (28.7% of head height) by 20px per side, and the repo's own trace records earLine proudPctOfHead 10.3 - delivered is 5.8% at the wrong latitude and 0% at the right one. Ears are BUILT (EarSpec/build_ear at line 541, radii 0.160/0.190) and in profile they do carry a rim and an inner concha shadow - this is a misbuilt, too-shallow, too-low ear, not a missing one. (2) THE PROFILE IS A FLAT WALL. In noodle-profile-review.png the entire face front from y153 to y200 sits on one dead-straight column at x=207 - that is the glasses ring seen edge-on with zero wrap - and the nose advances it to x=203 only at rows 200-211: 4px, 2.4% of the 165-row head band. The concept profile advances from x943 (lens line) to x959 (nose tip), 16px = 7.7% of its head band, three times as much. Credits: head depth/width 139/162 = 0.858 against the concept's 198/229 = 0.865, near-exact; NO severed rows in any of the four board renders (I ran a full row scan on front, profile, front-apose and profile-apose: zero rows with no figure pixels inside the bbox); legs are two legs. Held to 3 on the ear and the flat profile, plus the butt-joined shoulder wedge and the ankle 'napkin ring' called out below.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The numbers are in tolerance and I re-took them: head height 29.0% vs concept 31.0% (delta -1.99, ok), head width:height 0.99 vs 1.04 (delta -0.05, ok). The child proportion and the signature over-long thin neck read correctly and the neck sits organically into the skull with no collar seam. What holds this at 3 is the second half of the rubric line - 'joints read as connected forms'. Both shoulders fail it, and they fail it where a player looks: in noodle-runtime-hero.png the far shoulder carries a hard-edged navy wedge roughly 20x25px at native scale, outlined by the rim shader so it reads as a TEAR in the tee, and the near sleeve cap is a butt-joined tube pushed into the torso with a crease instead of a deltoid. The same wedge is present and larger in noodle-runtime-run.png, where the far shoulder reads as a detached dark lump with its own outline floating off the torso. The hand at run is a stack of hard-edged bars separated by black outlines rather than a fist. Torso mass is also thin against the head: A-pose shoulder span 146px against a 162px head, and the T-pose torso below the armpit runs only 72-86px, so the head is 1.9x the torso's width.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Abstained - null. NOODLE IS BALD; there is no hair mass to score and no hair surface is built (the script declares HAIR = #3A2A1C explicitly as an 'unused surface lane - he is bald; brows are atlas ink'). The bald negative space itself is intact in the board renders: one uninterrupted dome, no invented cap, no hairline seam, no hole. I did NOT run measure:strands, per the brief. One consequence of baldness belongs to other categories rather than here and is recorded there: because the crown is his own skin, the dome's faceting and its warmth shortfall land on the largest single surface he has.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I verified the edges are constructed rather than painted: scanning down x=268 through the tee, every stripe boundary transitions in 1-2px (329->331, 348->350, 371->373, 392->394, 416->418) - these are vertex-colour edges, not gradients. Rolled jean cuffs exist on both legs, band y572-592 = 3.6% of figure height against the concept roll's 4.4%, correctly placed at the ankle on both legs (TEAM_MASK, judged on extent and placement only - the untinted grey on the board and the tinted olive at runtime are both expected). Wrist cuff band, cream cupsole and two cream lace straps are all built (straps=((-0.170,-0.122),(-0.060,-0.012)) in NOODLE_SHOE). Held at 3 for four things. (1) THE SHOE IS NOT A LACED LOW-TOP. Cropped at 6x front and 7x profile, the two authored straps render as flat cream stripes on the outer quarter; there is no throat, no eyelets, no tongue, no collar opening and no separately readable toe bumper. The concept shoe has four lace crossings, metal eyelets, a cream toe cap and a dark chevron; the delivery is a tan clog with racing stripes. The rubric names laces explicitly. (2) The dark navy wedge at both sleeve/torso junctions reads as a hole in the garment at hero and run scale (see headBodyProportions). (3) The jean cuff is a smooth ring WIDER than both the jean leg above it and the shoe below it, with a hard step at each end and no fold edge - a napkin ring, not a rolled hem. (4) Garment warmth is largely gone: the cream stripe delivers rgb(210,207,202), r-b = 8, against the concept's rgb(229,208,183), r-b = 46 - 17% of the concept's warmth - and the blue stripe delivers b-r = 19 against the concept's 36. Denim itself is fine, rgb(74,103,137) vs concept rgb(52,78,105).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Below the floor, and the cause is a mis-traced landmark that the gate then certified against itself. THE MOUTH IS ~9.5 POINTS OF HEAD HEIGHT TOO HIGH. The repo's own machine trace, scripts/v2/turnaround-specs/noodle.spec.json, records landmarks.mouth = { value: 78.9, row: 288, confidence: 'traced' }. My own luminance map of the concept confirms it exactly: the smile is the dark run at row 288, and rows 261-264 - which the sculpt script and featurelatitude.lint.test.js both cite as 'the small smile rows 262-270' - are his NOSTRILS (the nose bulb runs ~245-264). featurelatitude.lint.test.js's own header warns about precisely this failure mode ('...NOSTRIL not the lip line, so it reports the mouth 10 [points] high'); Noodle's hand-entered mouth: 69.4 is that mistake hard-coded, so the record's 'mouth 69.4/69.4 green' is the sculpt agreeing with its own error, not with the drawing. On the delivered render the mouth line is row 207 of the 88->260 head band = 69.2% - faithful to the wrong target. THE CONSEQUENCES ARE THE WHOLE CATEGORY. The smile sits directly under the lens rims with no philtrum, and the nose has nowhere left to live: in noodle-front-review.png, cropped at 8x across x230-310/y185-245, the region between the lenses is UNMODULATED SKIN - no bulb, no nostrils, no cast shadow, only a scatter of freckle dots - against the concept's large highlighted button nose with two dark nostril slits. nose_push IS built (line 128, 'centre nz -0.42'), so this is a nose too shallow and too low, not an absent one: in profile it is a 4px hard-edged wedge at rows 200-211, i.e. AT the mouth's own latitude, and it projects 2.4% of head height past the frame line where the concept's projects 7.7%. Eye-to-mouth spacing collapses to 11.4% of head height (iris centroid row 187.5, mouth row 207) against the concept's 25.3% (iris 233.5, mouth 288) - 45% of the drawing's - leaving the features crammed in a band under the glasses and the bottom quarter of the face blank. The measured visible-face shortfall follows: 35.6/35.6 against 45.4/44.0, OFF by 9.8 and 8.4 on a tolerance of 6, and at that sample row the delivered head is crossed by irises (11px and 9px), sclera and four frame crossings while the concept's same row is 88.6% clean skin. Expression: all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are genuinely painted and distinct (295-296 KB each, no undersized sibling - grin shows a teeth band, cheer an open O, tongue a pink tongue, angry a closed line), but in ALL FOUR the eyebrows are hidden behind the lens rims at the gameplay camera, so angry and neutral differ only by a flat mouth stroke and angry does not read as angry. At hero the near lens reads as a dark socket and the temple bar is the boldest mark on the face.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives at hero - bald dome plus big round glasses plus blue/cream stripes is unmistakable from front, three-quarter and behind - and that is what keeps this off a 2. Two things hold it well below approval. (1) THE DOME IS VISIBLY FACETED. Cropped at 4x from noodle-runtime-hero.png, the skull shows large flat polygon facets with hard shading breaks across the crown and occiput, and the same faceting is present in every runtime still (run, swing_contact, and all four face cells). On the one character whose crown is his own skin and his largest single surface, this is the first thing the eye lands on. (2) THE SKIN LOSES ITS WARMTH BAND, which his record says is load-bearing for him. I sampled the delivered board's upper dome at (250,110) 40x20: rgb(225,203,179), r-g = 22, sat 0.20, and 0% of that patch passes the project's own isSkin test (it fails sat > 0.22). The concept's dome at (195,150) 40x20 is rgb(253,208,154), r-g = 45, sat 0.39, 100% isSkin. Cheek: delivered r-g 29 / sat 0.31 against concept r-g 70 / sat 0.58. Across rows 96-148 of the delivered front render only 30-41% of the head row classifies as skin, against 99-100% on the concept. At runtime the same skin renders ochre/mustard and drifts toward the infield dirt. At 40px (board strip, cropped at 4x) the bald pale head and the striped shirt carry, but the glasses survive only as a faint grey smudge - his one memorable cue is at the edge of legibility, leaving a single-cue read.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Boomer is THE big kid and the delivered silhouette is not a big kid. Normalising each figure to its own head-box width (concept ear span 1.153ft, delivered 1.238ft) the outer silhouette at z=0.8ft is 1.084 head-widths on the concept and 0.616 on the delivered — 57%. Raw ink at the same heights: 1.250 vs 0.655ft (52%) at 0.8ft, 1.445 vs 0.797 (55%) at 1.0ft, 1.742 vs 0.918 (53%) at 1.2ft. The belly recovers to 78% (1.353 vs 1.052 head-widths at z=2.0ft), so the torso is only modestly slimmed while the limbs are halved — the drawing's tree-trunk legs are pencils. The second identity, the mohawk, is a different FORM: the concept fan is one continuous forward-swept fin with feathered tips and no daylight in it; delivered is nine separate hard-faceted cones radiating like a stegosaurus frill with clean background between them (profile-review at 8x). Shoulders are a flat horizontal shelf with sleeve cylinders butt-joined onto it, their shaded end caps showing as dark notches inboard (front-apose at 8x) — the rubric's named 5/5 disqualifier, and here it costs more than the 5. Colourless, this silhouette reads as an average-build kid with a spiky crest, not as Boomer.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Head size is broadly right and its two OFF metrics have recorded causes I am not re-litigating (34.9% of figure height against 37.3%; w:h 0.87 against 0.77; the T-pose arm band at z 2.56 blocks the instrument's centre run). The A-pose board measures 33.6%, so the head is a little small but inside a fair reading. What fails is the second half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms'. The shoulder is a flat shelf, not a deltoid: in swing_contact at 10x the sleeve cap is a separate faceted ball with a hard silhouette break against the torso cone. The elbow (swing_contact, 5x) is a hinge between two straight tubes with no elbow volume and a visible crease facet. The knees have no form at all — the legs are smooth tapered cylinders from shorts hem to sock. And the limb-mass gap above (52-57% of the concept) sits against a nearly correct head, which is exactly the proportion error that makes him read as a normal kid with a slightly big head instead of the drawing's low, wide, heavy child. The neck is also longer and thinner than the concept's near-absent neck.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Strands, my own runs: default 5-45% band gives 89% of the concept's minima count at 305% of its prominence. I re-ran on a tightened 5-25% band, chosen to stay off the forehead and brows where skin/hair and brow edges register as FALSE creases — 103% count, 224% prominence (2-30%: 91%/244%; 10-40%: 90%/351%). So grouping is not the shortfall; the over-deep prominence is the spike GAPS being counted as creases, which is the honest reading of a crest built from separate cones. Two real failures. (1) The shaved fade stops at the temples. The concept carries dark shaved sides from the temple down past the ear on both front and profile; delivered has a thin brown band across the forehead and bare skin below it, so from the front and from any three-quarter angle the sides of the skull are naked — 3.3's 'no bare-skull read from any gameplay angle'. Measured, hair covers 33.3% of the delivered head box against the concept's 41.5% (80%), and it is 10-18% narrower relative to head height through its lower half (width/headH at t=20/25/30% down: concept 40.4/44.5/49.4%, delivered 36.0/36.0/41.3%). (2) The stubble/skin boundary is a stair-stepped zigzag at loft-ring resolution — visible without magnification in boomer-profile-review and violently so in swing_contact, where it also carries an isolated skin-coloured island inside the dark field. That is a torn edge, not a fade line. The mohawk itself is not one designed mass, it is nine cones on a cap.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I credit it: a cream sleeve cuff, a shorts hem, and a genuine shoe with a cream cupsole, a ground-line welt and a toe cap. Against that: no laces — the delivered shoe has one dark V notch where the concept has cream flat laces criss-crossed through eyelets over a navy tongue (12x, both); two cream side stripes that are not in the drawing at all; and a ragged, mottled toe-cap boundary against the navy. The socks are smooth tubes; the concept's crew socks are heavily ribbed with a rolled top, and none of that ribbing survived. The sleeve is a cylinder butt-joined to the shoulder shelf with its end cap visible. And the garment that IS his identity is washed out: measured over the shirt rows, concept gold rgb(235,160,46) sat 80.6% and cream rgb(251,230,192) sat 23.3%; delivered gold rgb(209,171,116) sat 44.3% and cream rgb(208,203,194) sat 6.4% — the cream stripe has gone neutral grey. Gold-to-cream luminance contrast, which is lighting-robust because both are read inside one image, is 28.3 against the concept's 63.6 — 44%. (Lighting is still a partial confound between a render and a drawing, so treat the ratio, not the absolutes.) TEAM_MASK extent on the sock roll-top looks correct; I am judging extent, not colour.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The four expression cells are the best thing on this asset and I am scoring them up: grin, cheer, tongue and angry all read at draft-card distance with real lips, an upper tooth band, a red tongue and brows that genuinely change — 3.14 passes cleanly on the fresh stills. Three things hold it under 4. (1) There is no nose from the front. nose_push exists in the sculpt source (line 122) so it is built, but head-on it produces no shading break whatever, and the face plate between the eyes and mouth is blank orange at hero zoom (cheer, 4x). In profile it is the wrong shape too: measured, the delivered face edge advances 17px — 9.0% of its 189px head height — over only ~10 rows, where the concept advances ~10px (4.1% of its 245px head) spread over ~45 rows. A soft button became a thin beak, 2.2x as proud and ~3.5x as narrow. (2) It is a sticker on a sphere: no jaw, no chin, no cheek planes, and the mouth decal's lower lip overruns the chin line onto the jaw. (3) It does not survive yaw. In the FRESH hero (idle f52) and run stills the head is turned ~60-70 degrees and the flat atlas leaves one eyebrow plus a hooked white crescent of sclera pinned to the silhouette edge, with the far eye and the entire mouth off-model. faceAsymmetry measures 0.00 both sides, so the spike/lean x offsets do sum to zero as the record requires; the visible-face-left OFF is the sheet's own 8.4 lighting split and I am not re-litigating it.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Both ends fail on evidence that post-dates the model (GLB 18:44:27, stills 19:00:33-19:00:55). HERO: boomer-runtime-hero is the designated close-up and it has no readable face — the head is yawed away, and at 5x the read is a blank orange ball with one dark brow bar and a white hook of sclera jammed on the right silhouette edge, no mouth anywhere. WHAT REMAINS, and it is the half the finding named: peaches-front-apose-review.png (190,240 70x70) and (290,240 70x70) at 8x still show a discrete skin ball with a dark concave shadow crease under it where it meets the arm cylinder, and a hard step where the ball's outboard silhouette drops onto the arm; the runtime stills still read it as a knob on a stick (face-angry 455,300 150x80; run 480,300; hero 470,300). Cause is unchanged: the dome at source line 733 has radii 0.098/0.108/0.102 while the arm's first skin stations are 0.080-0.090, so the ball overhangs the arm by ~0.015-0.02 ft all round and the lighting draws the overhang as a crease. The root ring is body-side geometry and cannot touch that; the tune is to taper the dome into the 0.090 ring (or grow the first two arm stations to meet it).
